outcome: Maternal satisfaction with labor and delivery care services
cohort: 593 mothers who gave birth at the University of Gondar Teaching Hospital, Ethiopia between July and September 2016
finding: The level of satisfaction with labor and delivery care services was poor (31.3%), with rural residency and chronic medical co-morbidity being negatively associated, while travel time, mode of delivery, and payment-free delivery service had a positive influence.
mod_finding: Birth by episiotomy or assisted vaginal delivery was positively associated with maternal satisfaction.
